Rashi on Ketubot 18a:2:2.english: [He is] deemed credible - By Torah law, without an oath.

Rashi on Ketubot 18a:3:1.hebrew: וניתני מודה ר' יהושע כו' והאכלתיו פרס - פרעתיו חציו, שהוא נאמן בלא שבועה הואיל ואין שור שחוט לפניו, דאשמועינן רבותא, דאע"ג דמודה במקצת פטור הואיל ואינו תובעו:
Rashi on Ketubot 18a:3:1.english: And let [the Mishnah] teach: Rabbi Yehoshua concedes, etc., and I fed him half - I paid him half of it, [teaching] that he is believed without an oath since there is no "slaughtered ox before him"; for [this] would teach us a novelty, that even though he admits to part [of the debt], he is exempt [from an oath] since [the heir] is not suing him.

Rashi on Ketubot 18a:4:1.hebrew: אליבא דמאן - תנאי פליגי בהא מילתא בשבועות (דף מב.), ואי אמר רבי יהושע הכי, לא כחד מנייהו הוא. דאי כרבנן, הא אמרי אפי' תובעו וזה מודה במקצת, משיב אבידה הוא, דתנן בשבועות: "מנה לאבא בידך", "אין לך בידי אלא חמשים דינר" — פטור, משום שהוא כמשיב אבידה; ומאי אשמעינן רבי יהושע באין שור שחוט? אפי' שור שחוט לפניו נמי נאמן. ואי אליבא דר' אליעזר בן יעקב, כי לא תבע ליה נמי, האמר שבועה בעי:
Rashi on Ketubot 18a:4:1.english: In accordance with whose [opinion] - Tannaim disagree about this matter in Shevuot (42a), and if Rabbi Yehoshua said this, it is not in accordance with either of them. For if [it is] according to the Rabbis, they say [that] even [when the heir] makes a claim against him and this [defendant] admits to part [of the claim], he is [considered] one returning a lost article, as we learned in a Mishnah in Shevuot: "[If one says,] 'My father had a maneh in your possession,' [and the other replies,] 'You only have fifty dinars in my possession,' he is exempt [from an oath], because he is like one returning a lost article." So what does Rabbi Yehoshua teach us in [a case where] there is no slaughtered ox [before him]? Even [where] a slaughtered ox is before him, he is also believed. And if [it is] according to Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov, even when [the claimant] did not make a claim against him, he says he requires an oath.

Rashi on Ketubot 18a:6:1.hebrew: ורבי אליעזר לית ליה משיב אבידה פטור - מן השבועה, בתמיה? הא תקנתא דרבנן היא במס' גיטין (דף מח:): "המוצא מציאה לא ישבע מפני תיקון העולם". וכיון דכי אינו תובעו נמי מחייב ליה שבועה, הרי אין לך משיב אבידה גדולה מזה, וחייב:
Rashi on Ketubot 18a:6:1.english: And does Rabbi Eliezer not hold [that] one who returns a lost article is exempt - From the oath, [asked] in astonishment! For it is a rabbinic enactment in Tractate Gittin (48b): "One who finds a lost article shall not take an oath, for the betterment of the world." And since even when [the claimant] does not make a claim against him, [Rabbi Eliezer] still obligates him in an oath, behold, you have no greater [instance of] returning a lost article than this, and yet he is obligated [to swear].

Rashi on Ketubot 18a:6:2.english: One does not take an oath on the claim of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor - It is a Mishnah in [Tractate] Shevuot.

Rashi on Ketubot 18a:7:1.hebrew: טענת אחרים הוא - ומאי פעמים דקאמר, ומאי טענת עצמו:
Rashi on Ketubot 18a:7:1.english: It is the claim of others - And what [is the meaning of] "there are times" that [the baraita] says, and what [is the meaning of] "his own claim"?

Rashi on Ketubot 18a:9:1.hebrew: אלא הכא בדרבה קא מיפלגי - אלא לעולם בטוענו קטן, ודקשיא לך: אין נשבעין על טענת קטן — הני מילי בשטוענו קטן "אני נתתיו לך", וקרא כתיב: "כי יתן איש אל רעהו", ולא קטן, ומהכא יליף לה בשבועות. אבל הכא שבא בטענת אביו, אית ליה לרבי אליעזר בן יעקב נשבעין; ורבנן פליגי עליה אפילו בטוענו גדול, וקרו ליה משיב אבידה, ובדרבה קא מיפלגי:
Rashi on Ketubot 18a:9:1.english: Rather, here they disagree with regard to [the statement of] Rabba - Rather, actually [the case is] where a minor claims from him. And as for what was difficult for you — [namely, that] one does not take an oath upon the claim of a minor — that applies only where a minor claims from him, "I gave it to you," and Scripture writes, "If a man gives to his neighbor," and not a minor, and from here [the Gemara] derives it in [tractate] Shevuot. But here, where he comes with his father's claim, Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov holds [that] one takes an oath; whereas the Rabbis disagree with him even where an adult claims from him, and they call him one who returns a lost object, and they disagree with regard to [the statement of] Rabba.

Tosafot on Ketubot 18a:1:1.hebrew: דסתם יהודה וגליל כשעת חירום דמי - תימה, דבריש גיטין (דף ד: ושם) תנן דבארץ ישראל אצ"ל "בפני נכתב ובפני' נחתם", אפי' מיהודה לגליל, משום דאיכא עולי רגלים ובתי דינין ועדים מצויין לקיימו. ויש לומר דהתם האשה מחזרת אחר עדי קיום; אע"ג דיהודה וגליל כשעת חירום דמי, תמצא עדי קיום כיון דאיכא עולי רגלים, אבל המחזיק אין רגיל לחזר אחר עדי מחאה. ואם תאמר: התם דאמר "שאני בני מחוזא דניידי", וצריך לומר אפי' באותה שכונה "בפני נכתב" דאין עדים מצויין לקיימו — אטו במחוזא לא תועיל מחאה שלא בפניו? וי"ל דהתם דרך הליכתן מן העיר כששמעו מחאה, רגילות הוא לומר: "פלוני מיחה", ושומעין אחרים עד שנשמע הקול למחזיק; אבל גבי גט, אין רגיל שיאמרו בהליכתן: "אנו חתמנו על הגט [או מכירין אנו חתימת עדים החתומים]":
Tosafot on Ketubot 18a:1:1.english: For standard [conditions between] Judea and the Galilee are like a crisis period - It is astonishing, for at the beginning of Gittin (4b and there [in the Gemara]) we learned [in the Mishnah] that in the Land of Israel one does not need to say, "It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence," even from Judea to the Galilee, because there are festival pilgrims, courts, and witnesses readily available to uphold [the document]. And one can say that there [regarding a bill of divorce] the woman goes around seeking witnesses to uphold [it]; even though Judea and the Galilee are like a crisis period, she will find witnesses to uphold [it] since there are festival pilgrims. However, the one who holds possession [of the land] is not accustomed to go around seeking witnesses of a protest. And if you should ask: There, where [the Gemara] says, "The residents of Mechoza are different, as they travel around," and [therefore] one must say "It was written in my presence" even in the same neighborhood because witnesses are not readily available to uphold it — is it possible that in Mechoza a protest [made] not in his presence would not be effective? And one can say that there, as they travel away from the city after hearing a protest, it is customary [for them] to say, "So-and-so protested," and others hear [it] until the report reaches the one holding possession; however, regarding a bill of divorce, it is not customary that they say as they travel, "We signed on the bill of divorce [or we recognize the signature of the witnesses who signed]."

Tosafot on Ketubot 18a:2:1.hebrew: אין צריך לפרעו בעדים - ואם תאמר: למאן דאמר צריך לפרעו בעדים, תקשי ליה מתניתין דהכא, דליתני "מנה לך בידי"? ויש לומר: דפלוגתא דתנאי היא בפרק שבועת הדיינין (שבועות דף מא:). אי נמי, דלא חשיב לה פירכא, דניחא ליה לאשמועינן דאין מחזיקין בנכסי קטן. ואם תאמר: מאי משני? אכתי ליתני: "ואם יש עדים ואמר לו אל תפרעני אלא בפני פלוני ופלוני — אינו נאמן"! וי"ל, דלא היה רוצה להאריך בלשונו, או שמא מילתא דפשיטא הוא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 18a:2:1.english: [He] need not repay him in [the presence of] witnesses - And if you ask: According to the one who says [that] one must repay him in [the presence of] witnesses, our Mishnah here should pose a difficulty to him — for let it teach [the case of] "You have a maneh in my hand"? And one can answer that it is a dispute of Tannaim in the chapter [entitled] Shevuat HaDayyanin (Shevuot 41b). Alternatively, he does not consider it a difficulty, because [the Tanna] preferred to teach us that one cannot establish presumptive ownership [chazakah] in the property of a minor. And if you ask: What does [the Gemara] answer? Still, let [the Mishnah] teach: "And if there are witnesses, and he said to him, 'Do not repay me except in the presence of so-and-so and so-and-so,' he is not believed"! And one can answer that [the Tanna] did not want to lengthen his wording, or perhaps it is an obvious matter:

Tosafot on Ketubot 18a:4:1.hebrew: אי אליבא דרבנן הא אמרי משיב אבידה הוי - כדמסיק דבבנו מעיז, וא"כ לא מצי למיתני "ואם יש עדים אינו נאמן", דלעולם נאמן במגו דאי בעי אמר "פרעתי הכל", דבבנו מעיז ומעיז:
Tosafot on Ketubot 18a:4:1.english: "If [it is] in accordance with the Rabbis, didn't they say he is [like] one returning a lost article?" - As [the Gemara] concludes, [their reasoning is] that toward [the creditor's] son he is brazen; and if so, [the Mishnah] could not teach, "and if there are witnesses, he is not believed," for he would always be believed through a migo [since he could have made a stronger claim], as if he wanted, he could have said, "I repaid everything," for toward [the creditor's] son he is certainly brazen.

Tosafot on Ketubot 18a:6:1.hebrew: ורבי אליעזר בן יעקב ליתליה משיב אבידה פטור - פי' בקונטרס: התנן "המוצא מציאה לא ישבע מפני תיקון העולם", ואית ספרים דגרסי הכי בהדיא. ואין נראה לרבינו יצחק, דמשיב אבידה פטור מדאורייתא מטעם מגו, ולא מכח ההיא משנה פריך, אלא פריך: "וכי לית ליה מגו?". וכן משמע בהניזקין (גיטין דף נא. ושם), דפריך: "ולית ליה לרבי יצחק המוצא מציאה כו'", ומשני: "הוא דאמר כר"א בן יעקב דאמר פעמים שאדם נשבע וכו'", ופריך: "ור"א בן יעקב לית ליה משיב אבידה פטור?". והשתא אי מכח מתני' פריך, הוה ליה למימר "ולית ליה לר"א בן יעקב המוצא מציאה", כדקאמר ארבי יצחק! ועוד, כיון דמשני "הוא דאמר כר"א בן יעקב", א"כ רוצה לומר דר"א פליג אמתניתין; א"כ מאי פריך "ור"א בן יעקב לית ליה משיב אבידה פטור"? אין הכי נמי דלית ליה! אלא מכח מגו פריך, כדפרישית:
Tosafot on Ketubot 18a:6:1.english: And does Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov not hold [that] one who returns a lost item is exempt? - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: Have we not learned in a Mishnah: "One who finds a lost item shall not take an oath, for the betterment of the world"? And there are texts [of the Gemara] that explicitly have this reading. But this does not appear [correct] to Rabbeinu Yitzchak, for one who returns a lost item is exempt by Torah law by reason of migo, and [the Gemara] is not raising an objection from that Mishnah; rather, it is asking: "Does he not accept migo?" And so it is implied in [the chapter] HaNizakin (Gittin 51a and there), where [the Gemara] asks: "Does Rabbi Yitzchak not hold [of the Mishnah] 'One who finds a lost item, etc.'?" And it answers: "He holds like Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, who says: Sometimes a person takes an oath, etc." And it asks: "And does Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov not hold [that] one who returns a lost item is exempt?" Now, if [the Gemara] were raising an objection from the Mishnah, it should have said, "And does Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov not hold [of] 'One who finds a lost item,'" just as it said regarding Rabbi Yitzchak! Furthermore, since it answers, "He holds like Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov," if so, it means to say that Rabbi Eliezer disagrees with the Mishnah; if so, why does it ask, "And does Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov not hold [that] one who returns a lost item is exempt"? Indeed, it is true that he does not hold [of it]! Rather, it is raising the objection on the basis of migo, as I have explained.

Tosafot on Ketubot 18a:9:1.hebrew: אלא הכא בדרבה קא מיפלגי - פירש בקונטרס: לעולם בטוענו קטן, ודקא קשיא לך: "הא אין נשבעין על טענת קטן" — ה"מ בבא בטענת עצמו, אבל בבא בטענת אביו טענה חשובה היא. וכי תימא: מ"ט דרבנן? דאין סברא לומר דסברי דאף בבא בטענת אביו לית ביה ממשא — אלא בדרבה קמיפלגי. ונראה דמשום דקרי ליה "טענת עצמו", דחקו להעמיד בטוענו קטן. אבל קשה, דעיקר התירוץ חסר מן הספר. ועוד, דבהגוזל קמא (ב"ק דף קו: ושם) ממעטינן: "נתנו כשהוא קטן ותבעו כשהוא גדול" — עד שתהא תביעה ונתינה שוין בגדלות; וה"ה דמהאי קרא ממעט "נתנו כשהוא גדול ותבעו כשהוא קטן", דהיינו כגון שנתן לו אביו ותבעו בקטנות. ונראה דה"פ: לעולם בגדול מיירי, אלא לא תימא דקרי ליה "טענת עצמו" משום דהודאת עצמו היא, אלא בדרבה קמיפלגי; ולרבנן, דסברי דבבנו מעיז — טענת עצמו היא. וה"ק ראב"י: פעמים שאדם נשבע על מה שאתם מחשיבים טענת עצמו, אבל לדידי, דאינו מעיז — טענת אחרים היא. ובסוף שבועת הדיינין (שבועות דף מב. ושם) דתנן: "אבל נשבעין לקטן", ומפרש: "בבא בטענת אביו, וראב"י היא" — ההוא "קטן" נמי לאו דווקא, אלא גדול, וקרי ליה "קטן" משום דלגבי מילי דאבוה קטן הוא, כדמפרש הכא. וקשה קצת, דהוה ליה לאקשויי ולשנויי אמתניתין דהתם כמו שמקשה על רב, דבההיא שמעתא גופה לא מקשה על המשנה אלא על רב:
Tosafot on Ketubot 18a:9:1.english: Rather, here they disagree with regard to Rabba's [statement] - Rashi explained: Actually, [the Gemara refers to] a case where a minor makes a claim against him; and as for your difficulty, "But one does not take an oath on the claim of a minor!" — that applies only when he comes with his own claim, whereas when he comes with his father's claim, it is a significant claim. And if you will say, what is the Rabbis' reason — for it is not logical to say that they hold that even when he comes with his father's claim it has no substance — rather, they disagree regarding Rabba's [principle]. And it appears [to Tosafot] that because [the baraita] calls it "his own claim," it forced [Rashi] to establish [the Gemara] as referring to a minor making a claim. However, this is difficult, because the main part of the resolution is missing from the text [of the Gemara]. And furthermore, in [the chapter] HaGozel Kama (Bava Kamma 106b and there), we exclude [a case where] he gave it when he was a minor and claimed it when he was an adult, [deriving] that the claim and the giving must both be in adulthood; and the same applies that from that verse one excludes [a case where] he gave it when he was an adult and claimed it when he was a minor — which is precisely such a case as when his father gave it to him and he claimed it during his minority. And it appears [to Tosafot] that this is its explanation: Actually, it is speaking of an adult; however, do not say that [the baraita] calls it "his own claim" because it is his own admission, rather they disagree regarding Rabba's [principle]. And according to the Rabbis, who hold that toward his [creditor's] son a person is insolent, it is [considered] "his own claim." And this is what Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov is saying: "There are times when a person takes an oath on what you consider his own claim — whereas according to me, since he is not insolent [even toward the son], it is the claim of others." And at the end of [the chapter] Shevuat HaDayyanin (Shevuot 42a and there), where we learned in the Mishnah: "But one takes an oath to a minor," and [the Gemara] explains: "[It refers to one] coming with his father's claim, and it is [the view of] Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov" — that "minor" is also not literal, rather [it means] an adult, and it calls him a "minor" because with respect to his father's matters he is [like] a minor, as [the Gemara] explains here. And it is somewhat difficult, for [the Gemara there] should have raised the objection and answered it regarding the Mishnah there just as it raises the objection against Rav, since in that very sugya it does not raise the objection against the Mishnah, but rather against Rav.

Tosafot on Ketubot 18a:9:2.hebrew: מפני מה אמרה תורה מודה מקצת הטענה ישבע - אפילו לרבנן דר"ש דלא דרשי טעמא דקרא, קא בעי רבה שפיר "מפני מה אמרה תורה" כו': דאמאי לא מהימן בלא שבועה במגו דאי בעי כפר הכל, או נילף מהכא דלא אמרינן מגו? ומשני: דאין זה מגו, דאין אדם מעיז לכפור. ואף על גב דבפרק שבועת הדיינין (שבועות דף מ:) אמרינן: בכופר הכל משביעין אותו שבועת היסת, משום דחזקה אין אדם תובע אלא אם כן יש לו, ופריך: אדרבה, חזקה דאין אדם מעיז פניו בפני בעל חובו! ומשני: דאשתמוטי קמשתמיט — אלמא בכופר בכל נמי אדם מעיז לכפור, דאשתמוטי קא משתמיט כמו במודה מקצת — מ"מ קאמר הכא שפיר חזקה דאין אדם מעיז לכפור הכל כל כך, ולא הוי מגו, דיותר ברצון הוא מודה במקצת הטענה דאינו מעיז כל כך. אבל אין לפרש דרבה אתא לפרושי מפני מה אמרה תורה מודה מקצת ולא כופר הכל, וקאמר חזקה דאין אדם מעיז לכך נאמן כשכופר הכל; דאם כן, במקום שיכול להעיז אפילו כופר הכל חייב! ובסמוך אמרינן איפכא לרבנן: דבבנו מעיז, ופטור אף מודה מקצת הטענה משום דמשיב אבידה הוא, מגו דאי בעי כפר הכל. ואם תאמר: ומנלן דכופר הכל פטור? וליכא למימר מדאצטריך קרא לחייב שבועה בעד אחד מכלל דכופר הכל פטור, דהא איצטריך להיכא שמעידים שגנב לו והוא אינו יודע! אלא י"ל דגזירת הכתוב היא, ד"כי הוא זה" משמע דבעינן כפירה והודאה; ועוד: מודה מקצת יש להשביעו שחייב לו ממון שהודה, ועל ידי כך מגלגל עליו שבועה כעין גלגול, אבל כופר הכל נסתלק לגמרי ממנו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 18a:9:2.english: Why did the Torah say that one who makes a partial admission in response to the claim is required to take an oath? - Even according to the Rabbis of Rabbi Shimon, who do not expound the reason of a verse, Rabbah aptly asks, "Why did the Torah say," etc. — for why is he not believed without an oath by virtue of a migo, since if he wanted he could have denied the entire [claim], or [why should we not] learn from here that we do not apply [the principle of] migo? And [Rabbah] answers that this is not a [valid] migo, because a person is not so insolent as to deny [the entire debt]. And even though in the chapter Shevuat HaDayyanin (Shevuot 40b) we say regarding one who denies the entire [claim] that we administer to him a hesset oath because there is a presumption that a person does not press a claim unless he has [a valid claim], and [the Gemara] asks: On the contrary, there is a presumption that a person is not so insolent in the presence of his creditor! And it answers that he is merely trying to evade [him temporarily] — thus we see that even when denying the entire [claim] a person is insolent enough to deny, because he is merely trying to evade [him temporarily], just as in the case of a partial admission — nevertheless, [Rabbah] aptly states here that there is a presumption that a person is not so insolent as to deny the entire [claim] to such an extent, and it is not a migo, because he more willingly admits to part of the claim, as he is not [being] so insolent. However, one should not explain that Rabbah came to explain why the Torah said [that] one who makes a partial admission [is obligated to take an oath] and not one who denies the entire [claim], and [that] he is saying [that] since there is a presumption that a person is not insolent, therefore he is believed when he denies the entire [claim] — for if so, in a case where he can be insolent, even one who denies the entire [claim] would be obligated [to take an oath]! Yet shortly below we say the opposite according to the Rabbis: that toward [his creditor's] son he is insolent, and even one who makes a partial admission is exempt because he is [considered] one who returns a lost object, [by virtue of a] migo that if he wanted he could have denied the entire [claim]. And if you ask: From where do we know that one who denies the entire [claim] is exempt? And one cannot say [that it is derived] from the fact that a verse was needed to obligate an oath on [the testimony of] a single witness, [which implies] by inference that one who denies the entire [claim] is exempt — for that [verse] is needed for a case where they testify that he stole from him and he does not know [whether he stole it]. Rather, one can say that it is a scriptural decree, for "that this is it" implies that we require both a denial and an admission. Furthermore, [in the case of] one who makes a partial admission, there is reason to administer an oath to him because he owes him money that he admitted to, and through that [the court] imposes an additional oath upon him, akin to gilgul [devolution of an oath]; whereas one who denies the entire [claim] has completely dissociated himself from him.

Tosafot on Ketubot 18a:9:3.hebrew: חזקה אין אדם מעיז פניו - לא כמו שפי' בקונטרס בהגוזל (ב"ק דף קז.), דאין אדם מעיז לפי שעשה לו טובה שהלוהו, אבל בפקדון מעיז; דאם כן, בפקדון מודה מקצת נמי יהא פטור במגו דאי בעי כופר הכל. ובכל דוכתא משמע דמודה מקצת חייב בפקדון: גבי "עשר גפנים טעונות מסרתי לך" כו' (שבועות דף מב:), דמשמע דאיירי בפקדון, וגבי "סלע הלויתני עליו ושתים היה שוה" (שם מג.), וגבי מציאה נמי אמרי' בהניזקין (גיטין נא. ושם) דמודה מקצת חייב ולא מהימן במגו. אלא אור"ת, דהיינו כגון חזקה שאין האשה מעיזה פניה בפני בעלה, שאין לאדם פנים לכפור הכל. וריב"א פי': אין אדם מעיז היכא שחבירו מכיר בשקרו; ואין להאריך:
Tosafot on Ketubot 18a:9:3.english: There is a presumption that a person is not so insolent [in the presence of his creditor] - [This is] not as Rashi explained in [the chapter] HaGozel (Bava Kamma 107a), that a person is not insolent [toward his creditor] because he did him a favor by lending him [money], whereas with a deposit he is insolent; for if so, in [the case of] a deposit, one who makes a partial admission would also be exempt [from an oath] through a migo [claim], since if he wanted he could deny everything. Yet everywhere [in the Talmud] it is implied that one who makes a partial admission is obligated [to take an oath] in [the case of] a deposit: regarding "I entrusted to you ten laden vines, etc." (Shevuot 42b), where it is implied that it deals with a deposit; and regarding "You lent me a sela upon it, and it was worth two" (ibid., 43a); and regarding a lost object as well, we say in [the chapter] HaNizakin (Gittin 51a and there[abouts]) that one who makes a partial admission is obligated [to take an oath] and is not believed through a migo. Rather, Rabbeinu Tam says that this is like the presumption that a woman is not insolent in the presence of her husband — [namely,] that a person does not have the nerve to deny everything. And Riva explained: A person is not insolent where his fellow recognizes his falsehood; and there is no [need] to elaborate [further].
